cells.Set by: GitHub repository settings. `.github/workflows/bench-refresh-health.yml` copies it into the environment of job `reconcile`. The test `bin/slice-tests/test_bench_refresh_workflow.py` also sets it.
cells.Values and default: GitHub user names in the form that `gh issue edit --add-assignee` accepts. The script passes the text unchanged and does not parse it. Unset: the new issue `Slice cost-data refresh is unhealthy` gets no assignee.
cells.Effect: When `reconcile-health` creates the issue `Slice cost-data refresh is unhealthy`, it assigns the issue to these users. An open issue with that title only gets a comment. When the `gh issue edit` call fails, the script prints a `::warning::` line and continues. Job `reconcile` runs only on the default branch. A manual run also needs the workflow input `send_alert` set to `true`.

cells.Set by: GitHub repository settings. `.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml` copies it into the environment of job `publish`.
cells.Values and default: Reviewer names in the form that `gh pr edit --add-reviewer` accepts. The script passes the text unchanged and does not parse it. Unset: the refresh pull request gets no review request.
cells.Effect: After `upsert-pr` creates or updates the refresh pull request, it requests a review from these reviewers. The refresh pull request updates `config/test-benchmarks.json`. When the `gh pr edit` call fails, the script prints a `::warning::` line and continues.

cells.Read by: Job conditions of the Slice cost-data refresh and of its health check, and job `plan` of the refresh (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`, `.github/workflows/bench-refresh-health.yml`)
cells.Set by: GitHub repository settings. No file in the repository sets it.
cells.Values and default: Set the exact lower-case text `true` to enable. The job conditions test it with the workflow expression `== 'true'`. `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh validate-invocation` tests the exact text. Unset: scheduled runs of the refresh and of the health check skip all jobs. A manual refresh run works only as a dry run.
cells.Effect: `true` turns on the scheduled Slice cost-data refresh, the publication of its pull request and the scheduled health check. It also permits a manual refresh run that is not a dry run. Job `plan` copies it to `ROLLOUT_ENABLED`. Publication also requires a run on the default branch. A manual health check does not need the variable. A dry run is a manual run with the workflow input `dry_run` set to `true`.

cells.Set by: No file in the repository. The value comes from the GitHub secret settings.
cells.Values and default: Text of an SSH private key for the user `aptuser` on the APT server (the server that holds the Debian package channels). Unset: no default. `publish-deb.yml` declares the secret as required when another workflow calls it.
cells.Effect: `publish-deb.yml` copies it to `APT_SSH_KEY` for the step that lists the `testing` channel. Both workflows pass it as `SSH_PRIVATE_KEY` to the shared workflow `publish-apt.yml`. The shared workflow is `positron-ai/github-actions/.github/workflows/publish-apt.yml`. It is not in this repository. A channel is one package repository on the APT server, for example `unstable` or `testing`.

cells.Set by: GitHub repository secret settings. `.github/workflows/deb-smoke.yml` and `.github/workflows/publish-deb.yml` copy the secret into the environment of one step.
cells.Values and default: Secret login token for the APT server `apt.positron.internal`. The script writes the text unchanged after the word `login`. Unset: the script prints `FAIL: POSITRON_APT_LOGIN_TOKEN must be set` and exits with status 1. An empty value does the same.
cells.Effect: The script writes the token to a temporary file. It mounts the file read-only into the Ubuntu 22.04 test container as the APT login file `/etc/apt/auth.conf.d/positron.conf`. The script unsets the variable before it starts `docker`. The token is not passed as a container environment variable. A workflow that calls `deb-smoke.yml` or `publish-deb.yml` must pass the secret. A person who runs the script by hand sets the variable first.

cells.Read by: Steps `Wait for complete build plan` and `Acquire build plan` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`)
cells.Values and default: Nix store path of the form `/nix/store/<32 characters>-<name>`. The jobs set it from the output `store_path` of job `prepare-tron-build-inputs`. Unset: no default. The jobs `wait-for-lab-cache` and `tron-build` set it in their `env` blocks.
cells.Effect: It names the build plan (the Nix output with the build recipe and the tool environments). `bin/ci/nix-cache/wait.py` waits until the lab Nix cache holds it. `bin/ci/nix-cache/acquire.py` copies it from that cache. Text that is not a Nix store path stops both scripts with an argument error. Each script waits at most 2700 seconds (45 minutes). The lab Nix cache is the Nix binary cache at `LAB_NIX_CACHE`.

cells.Read by: Step `Set up build environment` of the 3 workflows that set it, `bin/ci/ci-run-benchmark.sh`
cells.Values and default: Version number of cabal (the Haskell build tool that builds ingest). The 3 workflows write `3.16.0.0`. The readers append the text to `cabal-`. Unset: `bin/ci/ci-run-benchmark.sh` leaves `CABAL_INSTALL` unchanged. An empty value gives the same result.
cells.Effect: The step `Set up build environment` writes `CABAL_INSTALL=cabal-<version>` to `GITHUB_ENV`. `bin/ci/ci-run-benchmark.sh` exports the same `CABAL_INSTALL` text for its local rebuild when `CABAL_INSTALL` is empty. `bin/ci/setup-ghc.sh` assigns its own `CABAL_VERSION=3.16.0.0` and does not read the environment. `ingest-coverage.yml` and two steps of `cmake-single-platform.yml` write `cabal-3.16.0.0` directly. The workflow comments ask to keep these places equal.

hints.problem: The rows record pinned versions: Python 3.12.7, uv 0.9.5 and cabal 3.16.0.0. README.dependencies.md already records the same three pins and the steps to change them. .github/AGENTS.md lists README.dependencies.md and README.ci.md as the files to update when a pin changes. After this change a routine pin bump must also edit README.environment.md, and no check reports a miss.
hints.suggested: In the 5 rows replace the version number with a pointer, for example in PYTHON_VERSION: "Python version text with major, minor and patch numbers. [README.dependencies.md](README.dependencies.md) records the pinned value." Keep TRON_HOST_MIN_TRON as it is: its default `2.0.0~1tc6` is recorded nowhere else.

cells.Read by: Steps `Build with coverage` and `Check built ingest binaries have no bare -N (regression guard, #3087)` of job `ingest-coverage` (`.github/workflows/ingest-coverage.yml`)
cells.Values and default: Options for cabal (the Haskell build tool that builds ingest). The shell splits the text at spaces. The workflow writes `--enable-coverage --disable-optimization --builddir=dist-newstyle/coverage/cabal`. Unset: no default. The workflow sets it in its top-level `env` block.
cells.Effect: The steps add these options to `$CABAL_INSTALL build` and `$CABAL_INSTALL list-bin`. The options turn coverage on, turn optimization off and set the build directory. The `make` steps of the same job use the make variable `COVERAGE_CABAL_FLAGS` of `ingest/Makefile`. The Makefile assigns that variable with `:=` and does not take it from the environment. Both places hold the same options.

cells.Read by: `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh`, inline steps of the 4 workflows that set it
cells.Values and default: Branch name. The 4 workflows write `${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}`, the default branch of the repository. The readers use the text unchanged. Unset: `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` uses `main`. An empty value gives the same result.
cells.Effect: `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` uses this branch as the base of the refresh pull request. The benchmark report steps pass empty text in place of `BASE_REF` and `BASE_SHA` when the pull request targets this branch. The refresh pull request updates the Slice cost data. `bench-refresh.yml` also passes `refs/heads/<value>` to the script. The script rejects a scheduled refresh on another branch. `bench-refresh-health.yml` passes it to `bin/ci/bench_refresh_health.py`. `cmake-single-platform.yml` and `gcp-nix.yml` set it for one step only.

cells.Values and default: `true` or `false`, from the manual run input `dry_run`. The steps pass it to `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` as an argument. Other text stops that script with `invalid dry-run state`. Unset: does not occur. Both jobs define it. A scheduled run gets `false`. The input default of a manual run is `true`.
cells.Effect: `true` marks a dry run of the cost data refresh (the workflow that measures Slice test times again). The job `refresh` skips the default branch checkout. It uses `config/test-benchmarks.json` of the measured commit as base. With `false`, a manual run stops unless the branch is the default branch and the repository variable `SLICE_REFRESH_ROLLOUT_ENABLED` is `true`. The job `publish` opens the pull request. That job tests the input `dry_run` directly, not this variable.

hints.problem: Two spellings of one name. 13 rows write "Slice cost-data refresh". `DRY_RUN` and `ENABLE_2X72` write "the cost data refresh". The hyphen form is right: the repository documentation and the issue title use it.
hints.suggested: In `DRY_RUN`, replace "a dry run of the cost data refresh (the workflow that measures Slice test times again)" with "a dry run of the Slice cost-data refresh (the workflow that measures Slice test times again)". In `ENABLE_2X72`, replace "to the cost data refresh (the workflow that measures Slice test times again)" with "to the Slice cost-data refresh (the workflow that measures Slice test times again)".

cells.Values and default: Text of the repository variable `SLICE_REFRESH_2X72_ENABLED`. Only the exact text `true` enables. All other text counts as not enabled. Unset: the job always defines it. An undefined repository variable gives an empty value. Empty counts as not enabled.
cells.Effect: `true` adds the runner class `2x72core` (one kind of benchmark runner) to the cost data refresh (the workflow that measures Slice test times again). Without `true`, a request for `all` refreshes only `2x96core`. The steps pass the value to `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` as an argument. Without `true`, a request for `2x72core` stops the job `plan` with `2x72core refreshes are disabled`. The request is the manual run input `runner_class`. A scheduled run requests `all`.

hints.problem: Two spellings of one name. 13 rows write "Slice cost-data refresh". `DRY_RUN` and `ENABLE_2X72` write "the cost data refresh". The hyphen form is right: the repository documentation and the issue title use it.
hints.suggested: In `DRY_RUN`, replace "a dry run of the cost data refresh (the workflow that measures Slice test times again)" with "a dry run of the Slice cost-data refresh (the workflow that measures Slice test times again)". In `ENABLE_2X72`, replace "to the cost data refresh (the workflow that measures Slice test times again)" with "to the Slice cost-data refresh (the workflow that measures Slice test times again)".

hints.problem: Two definitions of runner class. Text A, in `ENABLE_2X72` and `EXPECTED_RUNNER_CLASSES`: "(one kind of benchmark runner)". Text B, in `REQUESTED_RUNNER_CLASS`: "(groups of CI servers of one type)". B is the better text. A class is a hardware type (`2x96core`: 2 CPUs of 96 cores; `2x72core`: 2 CPUs of 72 cores). One `2x72core` runner has no `benchmark` label.
hints.suggested: In `ENABLE_2X72` and `EXPECTED_RUNNER_CLASSES`, replace "(one kind of benchmark runner)" with "(a group of CI servers of one hardware type)".

cells.Read by: The step `Quiesce and run full slice cost-data measurement` of the job `refresh` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`). The shell commands of the manual recipe in `doc/slice.md` also read it.
cells.Set by: `.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`. A person who follows the manual recipe in `doc/slice.md` sets it by hand.
cells.Values and default: Bitfile identity `<release code>@<year>-<month>-<day>`. The release code is 4 hexadecimal pairs joined by dots. The text comes from the repository variable `SLICE_EXPECTED_BITFILE_2X96CORE` or `SLICE_EXPECTED_BITFILE_2X72CORE`. Letter case is ignored. Unset: the bitfile identity is not compared. An empty value does the same. An undefined repository variable gives an empty value.
cells.Effect: `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` gets the value as an argument. `bin/ci/bench_refresh_bitfile.py` reads the bitfile identity of every FPGA card of the runner before the measurement. It stops with `bitfile mismatch` when the identity differs from this value. `bin/ci/bench_refresh_bitfile.py` also stops when the FPGA cards hold different bitfiles. That check does not need this value. The manual recipe in `doc/slice.md` reads the same name and stops when it is unset or empty.
